sections.label: Act passed in April
sections.summary: The Act, first passed in April, intervened in certain contracts in response to the COVID-19 economic shock.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Act, which was passed for the first time in April this year, was a major intervention in certain types of contracts, in response to the economic shock caused by COVID-19.

sections.label: Notifications for Relief and determinations
sections.summary: By 1 September 2020, 7,046 Notifications for Relief were served and 1,272 determination applications filed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As at first September 2020, 7,046 Notifications for Relief, or NFRs, had been served through MinLaw’s electronic system.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: There are others which are done manually which we are unable to track in the system, and out of these, 1,272 applications for determinations by Assessors have been filed.

sections.label: Assessors, Registry staff, relief measures
sections.summary: The process worked well in most cases, with thanks to volunteer Assessors and Registry staff, alongside relief measures of about 100 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The process has worked well in most cases and I must say that we record our sincere thanks to the many volunteer Assessors, as well as the Registry staff who have come forward in the last few months to offer their services and who sat as Assessors in many of these cases.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These measures come on top of the various relief measures totalling approximately a 100 billion across four Budgets since May, including the Jobs Support Scheme, the Jobs Growth Incentive, as well as the COVID-19 Support Grant.

sections.label: Companies satisfied with relief measures
sections.summary: Surveys by three agencies found about 72% of polled companies were satisfied with the relief measures.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Based on these surveys, we gathered that approximately 72% of the companies that were polled by these three agencies said they were satisfied and happy with the relief measures that had been rolled out.

sections.label: Bill expands Assessors' powers
sections.summary: The Bill expands rental relief Assessors' powers to determine a wider range of matters, including rent waiver amounts under lease agreements.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Bill today expands the powers of the rental relief Assessors to allow them to make determinations on a wider range of matters in order to better assist landlords and tenants to implement the rental waivers in a fair manner.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Bill will empower the Assessors to determine the amount of rent to be waived pursuant to lease agreements.

sections.label: Reconciling Act with SOPA
sections.summary: Clauses 15 to 17 reconcile Part 8 of the Act with the Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Act, known as SOPA.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clauses 15 to 17 of the Bill reconcile the operation of Part 8 of the Act with the Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Act, commonly known as SOPA.

sections.label: Clause 15 relief moratorium
sections.summary: Clause 15 provides that an application for relief under Part 8 triggers a temporary moratorium on other legal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For example, clause 15 of the Bill provides that an application for relief under Part 8 will trigger a temporary moratorium on the commencement of other legal proceedings.

sections.label: SOPA adjudicator contract powers
sections.summary: The amendments give SOPA adjudicators the same powers to adjust contract terms as a Part 8 Assessor.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The amendments will also provide SOPA adjudicators with the same powers to adjust contract terms as an Assessor under Part 8 may have.

sections.label: Clause 12 delinks arrangements
sections.summary: Clause 12 amends section 27 to delink alternative arrangements from control orders, with intent to extend the Meetings Order to 30 June 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clause 12 therefore amends section 27 to delink the alternative arrangements from the control orders.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: With this amendment, we intend to extend the Meetings Order further, to 30 June 2021.

sections.label: Registrar discretionary rejection power
sections.summary: Clauses 5, 8 and 14 give the Registrar a discretionary rejection power on grounds including non-scheduled contracts, incomplete applications, and false or abusive applications.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clauses 5, 8 and 14 therefore provide that the Registrar will have a power, a discretionary rejection power on certain grounds.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: One, where the contract is not a scheduled contract, so it does not come within the ambit of the Act altogether; two, if the application is incomplete; and three, if the application is materially false or misleading, or frivolous, or is an abuse of process.

sections.label: Late payment interest cap
sections.summary: Clause 3 makes clear the cap on late payment interest applies to interest accruing from 1 February to the end of the prescribed period.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clause 3 makes clear that the cap on late payment interest applies to interest accruing from 1 February to the end of the prescribed period.

sections.label: Minister collective sale deadlines
sections.summary: Clause 19 introduces a new Part 9 empowering the Minister for Law to extend collective sale deadlines case-by-case by Ministerial Order.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clause 19 of the Bill introduces a new Part 9, that expressly empowers the Minister for Law to extend collective sale deadlines on a case-by-case basis, by way of Ministerial Order.

sections.label: Rental relief for SMEs and tenants
sections.summary: The Act is said to help individuals and companies, with 260,000 SMEs and over two million workers potentially benefiting from rental relief measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It would be good for us at this point in time, in this House, to appreciate and understand the positive impact of the Act in helping these individuals and companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I recall the hon Minister, Minister Shanmugam mentioning 260,000 SMEs employing over two million workers potentially stood to benefit directly from the rental relief measures alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Hon Minister, Minister Edwin Tong today mentioned about 7,000 notifications for leave has been filed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Similarly, in dollar terms, what is the estimated additional rental rebate that commercial, industrial and office tenants have or will receive from their landlords.

sections.label: Smaller landlords definition
sections.summary: Smaller landlords are individual or sole proprietor landlords with aggregate annual property value of $60,000 or lower as at 13 April 2020 and rental income forming 75% of gross income in Year of Assessment 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The smaller landlords are individuals or sole proprietor landlords whose aggregate annual value of their properties are equal to or lower than $60,000 as at 13 April 2020 and the rental income form 75% of their gross income in Year of Assessment 2019.

sections.label: Clause 8 updates section 19M
sections.summary: Clause 8 of the Bill updates section 19M on applying for an assessment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, clause 8 of this Bill updates section 19M on applying for an assessment.

sections.label: Registrar rejecting incomplete applications
sections.summary: Proposed subsection 8 lets the Registrar reject incomplete or non-compliant applications, with the current prescribed filing time being 10 days after the landlord receives a notice of cash grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the proposed changes to section 19M contained in this Bill, subsection 8 specifically enables the Registrar to reject an application if the application is incomplete or otherwise non-compliant, meaning if it is far later than the prescribed time or somehow does not conform to the manner specified.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, the prescribed time for filing an application for assessment is 10 days after the landlord receives a notice of cash grant.

sections.label: Accepting slightly late applications
sections.summary: The Registrar should be open to accepting applications that are slightly out of time or incomplete so as not to exclude meritorious applications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the Registrar should be open to accepting applications for assessments that may be slightly out of time or incomplete, so as not to exclude meritorious applications.

sections.label: Moratorium and contract modification
sections.summary: Clause 15 clarifies the moratorium applies to claims under SOPA, and clauses 16 and 17 allow contracts to be modified in a just and equitable manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Clause 15 clarifies the moratorium would apply to claims brought under SOPA and clauses 16 and 17 would allow the contract to be modified in a manner that is "just and equitable." And I acknowledge that this is the framework that has been used by Assessors dealing with all claims affected by COVID-19.

sections.label: Clarified legislation for adjourned meetings
sections.summary: The Minister clarified the legislation will remain in place until June next year, giving a long window of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, it was not clear the legislation would continue to apply to adjourned meetings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think it was very helpful the Minister clarified that the legislation is now going to be in place until June next year which gives a good long window of time.

sections.label: Feedback on alternative meeting arrangements
sections.summary: The provisions were well received, with feedback that the Companies Act should be amended to allow alternative meeting arrangements indefinitely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The second point that I would also like to make is, in fact, these provisions have been so well received that I have had feedback that perhaps the Companies Act should be amended to allow these alternative meeting arrangements to stay in place indefinitely.

sections.label: Sub-tenants missing rental relief
sections.summary: Some sub-tenants, especially coffeeshop stallholders, are not benefiting from rental relief as some landlords and tenants are not notifying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On my recent market walkabouts, I found that some sub-tenants, especially coffeeshop stallholders, are not benefiting from the rental relief framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is good that eligible tenants and sub-tenants do not need to do anything and, instead, the landlords are obliged to notify their tenants of the rental relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, I understand that some landlords are not notifying their tenants and some tenants are also not notifying their sub-tenants.

sections.label: Complaints about rental relief notification
sections.summary: The Member asks how many complaints the Ministry received about landlords or tenants not providing the two months of rental relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, can the Minister share how many complaints the Ministry has received with regard to landlords or tenants not providing the two months of rental relief that is supported by the Government to tenants and sub-tenants respectively?

sections.label: Alternative meeting arrangements expiry date
sections.summary: Current alternative meeting arrangements expire on 30 September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Current alternative meeting arrangements expire on 30 September.

sections.label: Assessor powers to specify waived rent
sections.summary: Under the new amendments, the assessor gets enhanced powers to specify the rent waived, reducing ambiguity and conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In particular, I note that under the new amendments, the assessor will be given enhanced powers to specify the amount of the rent to be waived.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: This will reduce the ambiguity and potential conflict between landlord and tenant, which will allow them to focus on their businesses.

sections.label: Amendment mediation for SMEs
sections.summary: The amendment aims to mediate and close issues with certainty, and residents say legal intervention has helped their small businesses with targeted solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The amendment will help to better mediate and close issues with certainty and reason.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: A number of residents have shared that the legal intervention thus far under the Act has helped their small businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: They appreciate that it is not a broad brush attempt but seeks to differentiate between the needs of SMEs and provide targeted solutions.

sections.label: PACT Registry assessors appointed
sections.summary: As of 4 September 2020, 298 assessors have been appointed to the PACT Registry and the rental relief panel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As of 4 September 2020, a total of 298 assessors have been appointed to the PACT Registry and the rental relief panel.

sections.label: 2020 property tax rebate amounts
sections.summary: The 2020 property tax rebate is about $1.8 billion and the cash grant component is about $2 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The property tax rebate for the 2020 period amounts to about $1.8 billion and the cash grant component, as announced by Deputy Prime Minister Heng at the Fortitude Budget, is about $2 billion.

sections.label: Landlord notice to tenants deadline
sections.summary: The Act mandates the landlord to pass a copy of the notice to tenants within four working days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng will know from the Act, it mandates the landlord to pass a copy of the notice to tenants within four working days.

sections.label: Notice passing and waivers
sections.summary: After receiving the notice of cash grant, the property owner must by law pass a copy to the tenant, and waivers kick in once the notice is received.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So four days to pass down the notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And after the notice of cash grant is received by the property owner, he is also required by law to pass a copy to his tenant and the framework is designed, as I mentioned earlier, in this case, once you receive the notice, then the waivers will kick in.

sections.label: Rental relief and revenue drop
sections.summary: Government pays the first one or two months, tenants get a further one or two months if they show a 35% revenue drop, comparing April and May 2019 against 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Government puts up the first one or two months, depending on whether it is industrial/office or commercial property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The tenants will enjoy a further additional rental relief of one or two months correspondingly, if they are able to demonstrate a 35% drop in revenue in the comparable period; and absent anything else it will be April and May 2019 against April and May 2020.

sections.label: Retiree landlord rental income relief
sections.summary: A retiree or small landlord whose rental income is 75% of annual income can apply for relief if no property has annual value over $60,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In the scenario where you might find a retiree landlord or a small landlord whose annual takings from rental income is a substantial portion of the annual income – 75% in this case – then that person can also apply for relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The qualifier there is as long as you do not hold properties where the annual value is more than $60,000.

sections.label: Alternative arrangements for year-end AGMs
sections.summary: The intention is to give companies planning year-end AGMs certainty they are covered by alternative arrangements, with long-term study of a permanent position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For the moment, our intention as I mentioned is to give certainty to companies who are planning for the year-end AGMs, some as far as six months down the road and we want them to know that they will be covered by the alternative arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For the long term, we will study it and if this is something that is useful and workable, we will consider whether or not and to what extent we can incorporate that into a more permanent position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These are steps that we gather as we encounter situations on the ground and we react to it by introducing amendments from time to time to this Bill.
